alert.title: Bug bounty #4471: other customers' orders visible via search

evidence.label: orders/search.py
lines: "SELECT id, total_cents, status, created_at FROM orders "
return jsonify([serialize_order(r) for r in rows])

question: Tap the line that lets the researcher read every customer's orders.

explanation.cause: status is interpolated into the SQL with an f-string instead of bound as a parameter.
explanation.why: `' OR 1=1--` closes the quote, ORs the customer filter away and comments out the rest, so the query returns all orders. customer_id and limit are bound safely; sort only ever comes from the SORT_COLUMNS allowlist. Fix: `status = %s` and pass status in the params tuple.
explanation.tell: The sort injection attempt returns a tiny normal response (allowlisted), while the quote-breaking status payload returns 48 KB: only the status value reaches the SQL text.

alert.title: Anomaly: one session fetched 3,812 distinct invoices in 9 min

question: Tap the line that lets one customer read another's invoice.

explanation.cause: The invoice lookup filters by id only, never by the caller's account.
explanation.why: requireAuth proves who the caller is, not what they may read. Any logged-in user can walk sequential ids and get other accounts' invoices (OWASP's IDOR / broken object level authorization). Fix: add `accountId: req.user.accountId` to the where clause so foreign ids 404 like missing ones.
explanation.tell: Requests from account acc_311 return 200 for invoices owned by three other accounts, in consecutive id order, and the only 404 is a deleted or nonexistent id.

alert.title: Audit: user.role changed member→admin with no admin actor

evidence.label: handlers/profile.ts
lines: export async function updateProfile(req: Request, res: Response) {
select: { id: true, displayName: true, avatarUrl: true, role: true },

lines.text: user.role u_77120 member -> admin actor=u_77120 via=PATCH /api/me

question: Tap the line that let a member make themselves admin.

explanation.cause: The update spreads raw req.body into Prisma instead of the validated parsed.data.
explanation.why: Zod objects strip unknown keys, so parsed.data could never contain role — but it is never used. The raw body goes straight to prisma.user.update, and role is a real column, so Prisma accepts it. That is mass assignment. Fix: `data: { ...parsed.data, updatedAt: new Date() }`.
explanation.tell: Validation passes because extra keys aren't errors, yet the audit shows role written from PATCH /api/me — a field the schema never lists.

alert.title: DLP: payroll CSV downloaded by non-HR user via /download

question: Tap the line that lets ../exports-hr through.

explanation.cause: The containment check is a raw string prefix match with no trailing separator.
explanation.why: filepath.Join cleans the path to /srv/exports-hr/payroll-2026-09.csv, which still starts with the string "/srv/exports". Escapes to /etc fail, so the check looks like it works. Fix: compare against exportDir + string(filepath.Separator), use filepath.Rel, or open via os.Root (Go 1.24+).
explanation.tell: Traversal to /etc gets 403 but a hop to a directory whose name merely starts with "exports" gets 200.

alert.title: Macie Policy:IAMUser/S3BucketPublic on exports-prod-7f3a

lines.text: PutBucketPolicy user=AssumedRole/platform-admin/jlee Deny Principal:* s3:* if aws:SecureTransport=false; Allow Principal:* s3:GetObject if aws:SourceVpce=vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f60718
PutBucketPolicy user=AssumedRole/platform-admin/jlee Deny Principal:* s3:* if aws:SecureTransport=false; Allow Principal:* s3:GetObject if aws:Referer like https://portal.example.com/*

items.value: off at bucket and account (static-site legacy)

question: Tap the call that made the bucket readable by anyone.

explanation.cause: A Principal:* GetObject grant conditioned only on aws:Referer — which S3 treats as public.
explanation.why: S3 calls a policy non-public only if it pins fixed values of keys like aws:SourceVpce, aws:SourceIp or a principal. aws:Referer isn't one: it is a client-supplied header anyone can set. The 09:02 policy was VPC-endpoint-only; the 09:11 rewrite swapped that for Referer. Fix: CloudFront with OAC plus signed URLs.
explanation.tell: Both policies say Principal:*, but only the second one swaps a fixed aws:SourceVpce for a spoofable aws:Referer, and Macie fires minutes later.

RunInstances region=sa-east-1 type=g5.12xlarge count=20 user=IAMUser/ci-deploy key=AKIA4XQ7EXAMPLE5RT2Z

question: What is burning the EC2 budget?
options: Long-lived IAM user key leaked publicly, used to mine crypto
Instance role credentials stolen from a web host via SSRF
Autoscaling policy misfire launching GPU nodes in DR regions
Compromised root console session launching fleet instances

explanation.cause: The ci-deploy access key, pushed to a public repo, was used to launch GPU miners.

Calls come from an outside IP minutes after the push, start with GetCallerIdentity, and hit regions you don't use. Deactivate the key, then terminate instances in every region and review IAM changes.

alert.title: GuardDuty: InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS (High)

items.value: hostname/IP denylist on the submitted URL only

question: How did the role credentials leave the instance?
options: DNS rebinding flipped an allowed host to 169.254.169.254
A dependency in the worker read creds from the environment
Allowed URL redirected to IMDSv1; client followed unchecked
IPv6-mapped address slipped past the hostname denylist

explanation.cause: SSRF: an allowed external URL 302'd to IMDS and the client followed it without rechecking.
explanation.why: The denylist runs only on the submitted URL, and the client follows redirects. With HttpTokens optional, a plain GET to IMDS returns role creds (IMDSv2 needs a PUT for a token first). Fix: require IMDSv2, recheck every hop, or block link-local in an egress proxy.
explanation.tell: Direct and IPv6-mapped tries are blocked; the 302 Location points at the IMDS credentials path, and the 1,342-byte reply matches a credential JSON document.

alert.title: auth-api: login failures 40x baseline, success ratio 0.9%

lines.text: login failed email=m***@gmail.com reason=unknown_user ip=91.214.x.x asn=AS9009
login failed email=d***@yahoo.com reason=invalid_password ip=176.59.x.x asn=AS12958
login failed email=t***@outlook.com reason=unknown_user ip=45.140.x.x asn=AS49505
login ok email=r***@gmail.com ip=102.89.x.x asn=AS29465 mfa=not_enrolled
login failed email=k***@gmail.com reason=unknown_user ip=187.19.x.x asn=AS28573

question: What kind of attack is this?
options: Password spraying: one common password across real accounts
Credential stuffing with pairs from another site's breach
Brute force cycling a wordlist against a few target accounts
Session store outage forcing users to log in again en masse

explanation.cause: Credential stuffing: another site's breached pairs, replayed via residential proxies.
explanation.why: Each email is tried once with one specific password; most emails don't even exist here, which a list built from your own users (spraying) wouldn't show. Brute force hammers few accounts and trips lockouts; an outage would yield mostly known users succeeding. Respond with breached-password checks, MFA and bot defenses.
explanation.tell: 68% of failures are unknown_user, one attempt per email, and ~1% of pairs work — the signature of someone else's breach list, not guessing.

alert.title: Egress firewall: catalog-search → 198.51.100.9:1389 (new dest)

question: What happened to catalog-search?
options: Internet scanner probing; the JNDI string was only logged
Logged User-Agent triggered a JNDI lookup to attacker LDAP
SSRF in /search let the attacker make the app fetch URLs
Compromised base image beaconing to a command server

explanation.cause: Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228): logging the User-Agent made Log4j resolve ${jndi:ldap://…}.
explanation.why: log4j-core before 2.15.0 performs lookups on logged messages, so a JNDI string in any logged header makes the JVM call the attacker's LDAP server, which can point it at remote code. Isolate the host, treat it as compromised, upgrade log4j-core (2.17.1+), and restrict egress.
explanation.tell: Under 100 ms after the UA is logged, the app host itself opens TCP to the exact host:port in the payload, then a second port. A probe that only gets logged makes no callback.

alert.title: build-runner-04: sshd CPU 4x baseline, SSH login p50 +500 ms

lines.text: Stopping ssh.service - OpenBSD Secure Shell server...
Started ssh.service - OpenBSD Secure Shell server.
Accepted publickey for ci from 10.8.0.12 port 40188 ssh2: ED25519 SHA256:q7Lw…

question: What is slowing sshd?
options: SSH brute-force bots saturating sshd with failed logins
Reverse DNS on each connection timing out before auth
OpenSSH switched to a costlier post-quantum key exchange
Backdoored liblzma hooking sshd's auth through libsystemd

explanation.cause: xz/liblzma 5.6.1 carries the CVE-2024-3094 backdoor, loaded into sshd via libsystemd.
explanation.why: Debian's sshd links libsystemd for service notification, and libsystemd pulls in liblzma. The malicious 5.6.x build patches symbol resolution as sshd starts, adding ~0.5 s to every connection — how Andres Freund found it. Rebuild the host from a known-good image and rotate its SSH and CI secrets.
explanation.tell: Login time steps from ~300 to ~800 ms the minute the liblzma upgrade restarts ssh, while OpenSSH, UseDNS and bot volume are all unchanged.

alert.title: Audit: refunds approved as role=admin by a member account

evidence.label: middleware/requireUser.ts
lines: export function requireUser(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) {
const claims = jwt.decode(token) as JwtPayload | null;

lines.text: token issued sub=u_8812 role=member jti=7c1e9a alg=RS256 kid=k2026-09 exp=16:21

question: Tap the line that lets an edited token through.

explanation.cause: jwt.decode() reads the token's claims but never checks its signature.
explanation.why: jsonwebtoken's README warns that decode "will not verify whether the signature is valid". Anyone can edit the payload to role: admin and keep the old signature, and the exp check still passes. Fix: jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["RS256"] }) and trust only the claims it returns.
explanation.tell: auth-svc signed jti 7c1e9a with role=member, yet orders-api acted on that same jti as role=admin: the claims changed after signing and nothing checked.

alert.title: Scanner burst on www: 2,310 probes from one IP, 4 answered 200

items.value: config/production.yml with SMTP and CMS keys until a 2025 commit

question: What did the scanner get?
options: Nothing: every sensitive probe 404'd, so this is just noise
The site's .env file, holding production environment secrets
A directory listing of the web root, exposing file names
The whole git repo, history included, from the web root

explanation.cause: The deploy copied .git/ into the web root, so the repo can be downloaded.
explanation.why: rsync -a ./ copies the checkout including .git/, and nginx serves dotfiles unless told not to. With HEAD, index and pack files anyone can rebuild the repo, secrets deleted in later commits included. Fix: deploy a build artifact, deny dotfile paths in nginx, and rotate every secret in the history.
explanation.tell: /.git/HEAD returns 200 with 21 bytes ("ref: refs/heads/main"), then config, index and a 48 MB pack also return 200, while /.env and the other probes 404.

alert.title: Bug bounty #6031: third-party page reads logged-in users' /api/me

evidence.label: server/cors.ts
lines: export function cors(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) {
// '*' broke login: Chrome refuses a wildcard when credentials are included

lines.text: The value of the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header in the response must not be the wildcard '*' when the request's credentials mode is 'include'.

question: Tap the line that lets any website read a user's /api/me.

explanation.cause: The middleware echoes any request Origin back as allowed, with credentials on.
explanation.why: The SPA needs Allow-Credentials, and browsers rightly refuse '*' with credentials. Echoing the request's Origin turns that into "every origin, with cookies", so any page a user visits can read their account data. Fix: echo the Origin only when it is on an allowlist (app.example.com); otherwise send no CORS headers.
explanation.tell: A request from Origin https://free-gift-cards.example gets that exact origin back as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, with credentials, and a logged-in user's data.

alert.title: Fraud: saved card used from a new IP minutes after owner's login

lines.text: session created sid=7f3c…a1 user=- ip=198.51.100.40 ua=python-requests/2.32.3

items.value: cookie, or ?sid= query param (legacy email links)
unchanged; not in any known breach corpus

question: How did 198.51.100.40 get into u_4410's account?
options: Stored XSS on a product page stole the logged-in session cookie
A phished password let the attacker log in as the user
Session id set before login was kept after authentication
Session ids are predictable and the attacker guessed one

explanation.cause: Session fixation: the app keeps the pre-login session id when the user logs in.
explanation.why: The attacker created an anonymous session, got the victim to open a link carrying ?sid=, and waited. Login attached u_4410 to that same id, so the attacker's copy became a logged-in session. HttpOnly can't help: nothing was stolen. Fix: issue a new session id at login and stop accepting ids from the URL.
explanation.tell: sid 7f3c…a1 was created from 198.51.100.40 six minutes before the victim logged in with it, and that IP then uses it without ever logging in.

alert.title: AWS WAF: blocked requests 40x baseline on api-alb

items.value: 18,402 distinct logged-in users, normal session ages
store rollout began 13:00; listing photos now inline base64 in JSON

question: What is the WAF blocking?
options: An attack campaign the WAF is correctly stopping at the edge
A bot network replaying stolen sessions against listings
False positive: app 5.12 bodies exceed the WAF's 8 KB rule
Origin 5xx errors miscounted as WAF blocks during the release

explanation.cause: A false positive: app 5.12 sends listing bodies over 8 KB, which the CRS size rule blocks.
explanation.why: SizeRestrictions_BODY blocks any body over 8 KB (8,192 bytes), and inline base64 photos push every 5.12 listing past it. Attacks vary payloads, rules and sources; this is one rule on one endpoint, hit by real users as the rollout grows. Fix: override that rule to Count for POST /v2/listings, or upload photos separately.
explanation.tell: Every block is SizeRestrictions_BODY on POST /v2/listings from ShopApp 5.12, sent by 18k logged-in users and rising with the rollout, while 5.11 requests pass.

alert.title: npm: @acme/sdk 4.2.1 published with no release run or tag

evidence.label: .github/workflows/pr-check.yml
lines: pull_request_target:   # needs write access to label the PR

lines.text: pr-check run #4821 event=pull_request_target PR #912 from fork ghost-dev-77/sdk (account 2 days old)
run #4821 step "npm ci && npm test -- --coverage" exit 0 (41s)
publish @acme/sdk@4.2.1 token=ci-automation (NPM_TOKEN) from a GitHub-hosted runner IP

items.value: automation token with publish rights on @acme/*

question: Tap the line that picks the fork's commit for this privileged job.

explanation.cause: pull_request_target checks out the fork's head commit and runs it with repo secrets.
explanation.why: pull_request_target runs with the base repo's secrets, which is safe while it runs base-branch code. Checking out head.sha swaps in the fork's package.json, so npm test ran the attacker's script with NPM_TOKEN in its env. Fix: test under pull_request (no secrets), keep pull_request_target for labeling only, and rotate NPM_TOKEN.
explanation.tell: A 2-day-old account's fork PR changes only package.json's test script; the pull_request_target run passes, and the CI npm token publishes 4.2.1 with no release run.

alert.title: DNS egress: CI runner queried 3,100 random subdomains of one zone

lines.text: runner-14 query 9f2c41….d.x7-metrics.example A NXDOMAIN (3,100 unique names in 4 min)

items.value: acme-ledger-client 2.4.1 is the newest; never had 99.x
project acme-ledger-client created 3 days ago, one release

question: How did the runner end up running someone else's code?
options: Typosquat: a misspelled package name in requirements.txt
Internal package index breached and a release swapped out
Public package with the internal name won on version number
Maintainer of a transitive dependency shipped a bad release

explanation.cause: Dependency confusion: pip found the internal name on PyPI too and took the higher version.
explanation.why: extra-index-url adds an index; it doesn't rank them. pip takes candidates from both and installs the highest version, so 99.0.0 on PyPI beats internal 2.4.1 (PyTorch's torchtriton incident worked the same way). Fix: one internal index that proxies PyPI, hash-pinned installs, and register the name on PyPI.
explanation.tell: Both indexes are searched, the name is spelled right, and pip installs 99.0.0: a version the internal index never had, from a PyPI project created 3 days ago.

alert.title: IAM user svc-backup2 created by role ci-deploy (a deploy-only role)

lines.text: AttachRolePolicy user=AssumedRole/ci-deploy/gha-8812 role=ci-deploy policy=AdministratorAccess errorCode=AccessDenied "…because no identity-based policy allows the iam:AttachRolePolicy action"
CreatePolicyVersion user=AssumedRole/ci-deploy/gha-8812 policy=ci-deploy-perms setAsDefault=true Allow Action:* Resource:*

items.value: "Let the pipeline update its own deploy policy"

question: Tap the event where ci-deploy gained the power it lacked.

explanation.cause: ci-deploy may write new versions of its own policy, so it rewrote it to admin.
explanation.why: The denied AttachRolePolicy shows the role was not admin. But iam:CreatePolicyVersion on its own policy lets it write any document, and setAsDefault makes it live: Action * on Resource *. Every later call just uses that power. Fix: never let a principal edit policies attached to itself; restore v3, delete the new version and svc-backup2.
explanation.tell: AttachRolePolicy is denied at 23:05; the next write is CreatePolicyVersion with setAsDefault=true on the role's own policy, and every IAM write after it succeeds.

alert.title: ATO: 214 accounts changed email, then reset password within 2 h

lines.text: accounts-web v8.14: session cookie SameSite=Lax -> SameSite=None; Secure (help-widget iframe on partner sites)

items.value: session cookie only; no CSRF token, no Origin check
each victim's usual home IP and browser
rotated at login; unchanged during the attack

question: How were the victims' emails changed?
options: Stored XSS on the profile page stole cookies to change emails
Cross-site POSTs ride the cookie; the form has no CSRF token
CORS misconfiguration let another site call the account API
Session fixation: attackers planted session ids before login

explanation.cause: CSRF: the email form trusts the cookie alone, and SameSite=None now sends it cross-site.
explanation.why: SameSite=Lax was the only thing stopping cross-site form POSTs, and it is a defense-in-depth layer, not a CSRF defense. Switching to None for the widget let any page submit the form with the victim's cookie. CORS only governs reading responses; nothing here needs one. Fix: CSRF tokens or an Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site check on state changes.
explanation.tell: The email changes come from victims' own IPs and browsers, but with sec-fetch-site=cross-site and a foreign Origin, starting after v8.14 set SameSite=None.

alert.title: Egress: invoice-import fetched files from a never-seen external host

evidence.label: InvoiceParser.java
lines: private static final DocumentBuilderFactory SAFE = hardened();
public Invoice parse(InputStream body, String contentType) throws Exception {

lines.text: org.xml.sax.SAXParseException; lineNumber: 2; columnNumber: 10; DOCTYPE is disallowed when the feature "http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl" set to true.
invoice-import-7d9 GET http://203.0.113.50/inv.dtd 200 (first contact with host)

items.value: JDK 25, default JAXP settings (no jaxp.properties overrides)
kept for one legacy EDI partner (p_022)

question: Tap the line that builds the parser behind the DTD fetches.

explanation.cause: The text/xml branch builds a default DocumentBuilderFactory without the DOCTYPE ban.
explanation.why: Only the application/xml path uses the hardened factory. Rejected there, the sender resent as text/xml, which gets a fresh default factory, and the JDK's default is to fetch the external resources a document names. Fix: route both branches through SAFE (one shared hardened builder) and block egress from the importer.
explanation.tell: p_ext91's upload is refused with the disallow-doctype-decl error as application/xml but gets a 201 as text/xml, and each text/xml import is followed by a .dtd fetch.
